title: Oregon Gun Laws Debated After Shooting as Rep. Bynum Says Babies Must Stop Dying
text:
Rep. Janelle Bynum discussed Oregon gun laws after a shooting, citing Measure 114 and saying we want our babies to stop dying on MS NOW's The Weeknight.
Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR) discussed Oregon gun laws on Thursday during an appearance on MS NOW's The Weeknight, following a shooting earlier that day in the state. Bynum said, we have said very clearly that we want our babies to stop dying.
The interview focused on Oregon's strict firearm regulations and the ongoing debate over Measure 114, a referendum-passed law that ranks among the nation's toughest.
Oregon Measure 114 Under Legal Challenge
Co-host Luke Russert noted that Oregon passed Measure 114 by referendum, establishing a permit-to-purchase system. He said Everytown, USA ranks Oregon as having one of the more stringent gun laws in the country.
Russert added that fringe groups are trying to get rid of the law in the courts, even though the citizenry of Oregon really wanted it. He referenced a recent mass shooting in Bend, Oregon, and asked Bynum to talk about how the state has responded.
Measure 114 requires a permit to purchase a firearm and limits magazine capacity. It was approved by voters but has faced legal challenges that have blocked or delayed its implementation.
Bynum Cites Children at Risk From Gunfire
Bynum responded by emphasizing the need to protect children. She said, we want our children to stop being shredded. We want people to stand up and ensure that when our kids are out, whether they are at the playground, whether they are at the grocery store, whether they are at community college, if they are at school, that they are not at risk for being shredded apart by gunfire.
She also highlighted the issue of interpersonal gun violence. As a black mom, Bynum said, she reminds people that we have interpersonal gunfire as well.
She stated that Oregon has taken steps to try and solve that, but we face people who do not want to face the music, and they are okay with our children continuing to die.
Oregon Gun Violence and Political Divide
The discussion comes amid heightened national attention on gun violence and policy responses. Oregon has been a focal point due to its strict laws and recent shootings.
Bynum's comments reflect frustration with opposition to gun control measures. She said we have said very clearly that we want our babies to stop dying.
The interview underscores the divide over gun regulations in the U.S., with Oregon serving as a key example of both legislative action and resistance.
